title: What CME and CPD do healthcare professionals need for a DoH license in Abu Dhabi?
seoTitle: DoH Abu Dhabi CME and CPD requirements
description: Department of Health Abu Dhabi CPD rules: annual credits by profession, the 50 percent formal rule, credit values, provider duties and portfolios.
shortAnswer: Licensed healthcare professionals in Abu Dhabi must earn the annual CME/CPD quota set by the Department of Health (DoH): 40 credits for physicians and dentists, 20 for nurses and pharmacists, and 10 for allied health and TCIM practitioners. Under DoH's CPD Standard, effective July 2024, at least half of each licensure cycle's credits must come from accredited formal activities, one hour equals one credit, and professionals must keep a CPD portfolio available for audit.
keyTakeaways: The Healthcare Professionals Manual (Part B, sections 72 to 75) requires every DoH licensed professional to obtain the required quota of continuing professional education each year and to maintain and submit CME hours on renewal.

The quota follows the Unified Healthcare Professional Qualification Requirements: 40 credits for physicians and dentists, 20 for nurses, 20 for pharmacists and 10 for allied health and TCIM practitioners.

The Standard for Continuing Professional Development (DOH/ST/HCWS/CPD/V1/2024) requires at least 50 percent of each cycle's credits from formal (Category 1) activities and allows at most 50 percent from non formal (Category 2) activities.
One hour of CPD equals one credit, the smallest unit is 15 minutes (0.25 credits), and teaching in a formal activity earns two credits per contact hour.
Healthcare providers must support staff CPD plans and portfolios, facilitate enrollment with measures such as flexible rostering, monitor progress and evaluate the impact of CPD on care.
jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates (Emirate of Abu Dhabi)

sections.heading: Which DoH instruments set CME and CPD requirements?

blocks.text: Three DoH documents and one federal standard work together. The Healthcare Professionals Manual sets the legal duty; the Standard for Continuing Professional Development (CPD) for Healthcare Workforce defines what counts and how credits are calculated; the CME/CPD Provider and Activity Quality Assurance Manual governs accredited providers; and the Unified Healthcare Professional Qualification Requirements (PQR) set the annual numbers. All are published on the DoH policies and standards pages ([DoH policies and manuals](https://www.doh.gov.ae/en/resources/policies)).

blocks.text: DoH, formerly the Health Authority Abu Dhabi, regulates the emirate's health system. Professionals licensed in Dubai follow different counting rules, set out in [DHA CPD requirements in Dubai](/regulations/dha-cpd-requirements-dubai). This page reflects the Abu Dhabi rules as at November 2026.

sections.heading: How many CME or CPD credits are required each year?

blocks.text: Section 74.1 of the Healthcare Professionals Manual requires each licensed professional to obtain, in each year of practice in Abu Dhabi, the required quota of continuing professional education, meaning training for a minimum number of hours and in subjects specified by DoH, delivered by a provider DoH accredits or recognizes ([DoH Healthcare Professionals Manual](https://www.doh.gov.ae/-/media/A47D9907918943438EDB512BE9347AB8.ashx)). Section 74.3 lets DoH set different requirements for different categories, and section 74.4 lets it exempt individuals or categories.

blocks.text: The PQR requires all CME/CPD to be relevant to the field of the specialty ([Unified Healthcare Professional Qualification Requirements](https://www.doh.gov.ae/-/media/D112FF75EF0140439A733B16081292DF.ashx)). Section 4.4.3 of the CPD Standard restates the professional's duty to obtain the required quota during every year of professional practice in Abu Dhabi.

sections.heading: What is the difference between formal and non formal CPD in Abu Dhabi?

blocks.text: Formal CPD (Category 1) is accredited, outcome based and assessed; non formal CPD (Category 2) is other relevant learning that DoH recognizes on lighter criteria. The CPD Standard requires at least 50 percent of the total credits for each licensure cycle to come from formal activities covering the professional's scope of practice, roles and responsibilities, and caps non formal activities at 50 percent ([DoH Standard for Continuing Professional Development](https://www.doh.gov.ae/-/media/66CD0B4E6BFE45818E20157A8A347773.ashx)).

items: **Accreditation (3.1.1.1):** a formal activity must be accredited by DoH, by a national accreditation body, or to a relevant international standard by a DoH approved international accreditor that is itself recognized in its home country. Completion of internationally accredited activities must be verified by DoH before approval.
**Assessment (3.1.1.7):** every formal activity must include an assessment, such as a quiz, observation or self assessment, of how far the learning objectives were met.
**Evaluation (3.1.1.8):** attendees must evaluate the content, presenter and delivery mode.

**Independence (3.1.1.3, 3.1.1.11, 3.1.1.12):** content must be free of commercial influence, any educational grant or commercial support must be disclosed to DoH and attendees, and delivery must be free of promotional activity.
**Formats (3.1.1.4):** live on campus, synchronous or asynchronous e-learning, blended learning, and other routes such as reading, writing, teaching and research.
**Non formal criteria (3.1.2):** relevant to the professional's role, adding value to knowledge and skills, and disclosing any commercial support.

sections.heading: How are CPD credits calculated for different activities?

blocks.text: One hour of CPD engagement equals one credit, 30 minutes equals 0.5 credits, and the smallest reportable unit is 15 minutes, or 0.25 credits (Standard definition 2.8). Appendix 1 of the Standard then gives credit rules and the proof required for common activities.

blocks.text: Credit bearing micro credentials count as formal CPD and must correspond to a level in the Qualifications Framework for the Emirates, ranging from 1 to 12 credit hours. Non credit bearing micro credentials count as non formal.

sections.heading: What must healthcare providers and CPD providers do?

blocks.text: Employers carry active duties, not just a records role. Section 4.2 of the CPD Standard requires DoH licensed healthcare providers to encourage and support each staff member's professional development plan and portfolio, facilitate enrollment through measures including incentives, financial support and flexible rostering, monitor progress toward CPD goals, and evaluate the impact of CPD on competence, performance and the quality and safety of care. Section 75.2 of the Healthcare Professionals Manual adds that providers should ensure their professionals obtain CME and keep written records.

CPD providers must be approved by DoH and hold a valid license in Abu Dhabi or the UAE (Standard 3.2). They need an institutional CPD policy, programs built on a needs assessment, qualified faculty, pre and post activity assessment where applicable, systematic evaluation and protection of learners' personal data. The Quality Assurance Manual adds that companies whose primary business is producing, marketing, selling or distributing healthcare products used on patients, such as pharmaceutical and device companies, are ineligible to be accredited as CPD providers, and that accredited activities must carry DoH's accreditation statement ([DoH CME/CPD Provider and Activity Quality Assurance Manual](https://www.doh.gov.ae/-/media/ED1BEEF92333440CB5C589D56EC7665D.ashx)).

blocks.title: Priority topics
blocks.text: Section 4.1.2 of the Standard lets DoH identify priority CPD topics that professionals must complete within a set timeframe, such as a licensure cycle, for example in a public health emergency. Facilities should watch DoH circulars so priority topics can be added to staff plans quickly.

sections.heading: What records must professionals keep, and how is CPD enforced?

blocks.text: Each professional must keep a CPD portfolio covering all four phases of the CPD cycle, with an up to date, accurate record of all activities, available on request for audit or monitoring (Standard 4.4.5). Appendix 2 describes the cycle as define, plan, complete and assess. Section 75.1 of the Healthcare Professionals Manual makes maintaining and submitting CME hours at renewal the professional's sole responsibility.

DoH monitors compliance through audit and inspection (Standard 4.1.4) and may impose sanctions for any breach under the disciplinary regulation of the healthcare sector (Standard section 6). The Standard was published in April 2024 with a revision period running to March 2027, so a revised edition may follow; check the DoH standards page before each renewal cycle.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each professional category, its quota and the formal and non formal rules as linked concepts, and attaches learning outcomes and assessment points to each activity before it is built. That gives Abu Dhabi providers the assessment and impact evidence the CPD Standard asks for, rather than attendance alone.

faqs.q: Is CME the same as CPD in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.a: The DoH CPD Standard notes that the terms are often used interchangeably and adopts the term continuing professional development. It defines CME as education that maintains or develops a physician's knowledge, skills and performance, while CPD covers the wider training of all healthcare professionals.

faqs.q: Can e-learning count as formal CPD in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.a: Yes. The Standard lists synchronous and asynchronous e-learning and blended learning as formats for formal CPD, provided the activity is accredited by DoH, a national body or a DoH approved international accreditor, includes an assessment, and is evaluated by learners.

faqs.q: Can a pharmaceutical company run DoH accredited CPD?
faqs.a: No. The DoH Quality Assurance Manual treats companies whose primary business is producing, marketing, selling or distributing healthcare products used on patients as ineligible to be accredited as CPD providers. Any commercial support for an accredited activity must be disclosed to DoH and attendees.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for proving CME hours at renewal in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.a: The professional. Section 75.1 of the Healthcare Professionals Manual makes maintaining and submitting CME hours at renewal the professional's sole responsibility, while section 75.2 expects employing providers to ensure their professionals obtain CME and keep written records.
